summary.headline: AEL reported record H1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA of INR 11,958 crore, up 56% YoY, with total income up 62% to INR 71,569 crore.
summary.overview: Adani Enterprises posted its highest-ever half-yearly EBITDA, driven by airports, copper, IRM and Carmichael mine coal earnings, as management framed FY27 as a shift from build-out to value realisation. Airport EBITDA rose 55% in Q2 to INR 1,641 crore, while copper ramped to 64% utilisation. Solar module capacity reached 10 GW and domestic module sales grew 35% YoY. Management declined to give numeric FY27 EBITDA or margin guidance and pointed to Q1-to-Q2 seasonality and the Navi Mumbai and toll-road ramp-up as the next drivers.

financial_highlights.value: Q2 INR 354 crore; Q1 INR 288 crore; H1 about INR 642 crore
Q2 about INR 470 crore; H1 INR 840 crore

segments.name: Airports (AAHL)
segments.commentary: Q2 passengers 21.3 million; total income INR 3,786 crore (+20% YoY), EBITDA INR 1,641 crore (+55%). Aero revenue +9% YoY, non-aero +57% YoY; H1 AAHL EBITDA INR 3,275 crore, close to FY25 full-year EBITDA.

segments.name: Data centres (AdaniConneX)
segments.commentary: New 240 MW hyperscale contract takes contracted capacity to 1.2+ GW. Operational capacity 94.6 MW after 29.2 MW handed over in the quarter; guidance of 120-150 MW by FY27 exit.

segments.name: Copper (Kutch Copper)
segments.commentary: Q2 sales 80.6 KT, utilisation 64%, revenue INR 14,843 crore, EBITDA INR 1,283 crore; management guides utilisation to 80-85% by FY27 year-end.

segments.name: Integrated Resource Management
segments.commentary: Q2 trading volume 7.4 MMT, revenue INR 7,169 crore, EBITDA INR 654 crore. Management gave no outlook given coal shortage.

segments.name: Mining Services
segments.commentary: Q2 dispatch 10.7 MMT, revenue INR 998 crore, EBITDA INR 407 crore. Management expects at least 10-15% higher volume than the end of last year.

segments.name: Adani New Industries (solar and wind)
segments.commentary: Module capacity expanded to 10 GW after 4.3 GW commissioned on 31 Aug 2026; domestic module sales 1,478 MW (+35% YoY); 35 wind turbine sets (+25% YoY); total income INR 3,669 crore, EBITDA INR 1,094 crore. Solar cell lines of 6 GW due by FY27 end.

segments.name: Roads
segments.commentary: Q2 EBITDA INR 354 crore, Q1 INR 288 crore, H1 about INR 642 crore. Ganga Expressway now operational; ramp-up slightly behind management's own estimates, attributed to monsoon and floods.

segments.name: Primary industry / PVC
segments.commentary: PVC plant at Mundra: 1 MMTPA, about INR 26,000 crore capex, about 60% spent; first part to commission next fiscal, with 6-9 months of stabilisation after full commissioning.

guidance_outlook: Navi Mumbai to exit FY28 (Q1 2028) at a run rate of 5 million passengers per quarter, against a maximum capacity of 20 million per year (5 million international, 15 million domestic).
Data centres: operational capacity of 120-150 MW at FY27 exit, then close to 500 MW over the next 12-18 months, billed as commissioned.
Group capex run rate of about INR 35,000-40,000 crore a year over the next couple of years, led by airports, data centres and PVC.
Copper plant utilisation to rise from 64% in Q2 to 80-85% by FY27 year-end; FY27 operating margin slightly higher, with a long-term band of 4-6% of revenue.
Mining Services volume to be at least 10-15% above the end-of-last-year level by FY27 year-end.
Solar module run rate of about 2 GW per quarter from the next quarter; 6 GW of cell lines by FY27 end.
Management declined to give FY27 EBITDA or margin guidance.
capex_capacity: Navi Mumbai Phase 2 Terminal 2 works to start November 2026; T1 redevelopment at Mumbai to start April 2027 (summer schedule).

Data centres: 1.4 GW under construction, of which 1.2 GW already tied up; funding split about 20/80 to 30/70 (equity/debt); capex per MW of INR 60-80 crore cited by an analyst, with management saying rates are broadly stable after pricing in cost increases.
Solar: module capacity of 10 GW completed (4.3 GW commissioned 31 Aug 2026); 2.2 GW ingot-wafer capacity in place, with the balance of about 8 GW to be built by 2028 under ALMM alignment.
Hotels (city-side): live at Ahmedabad by October 2029 and Mumbai and Navi Mumbai by March 2030; new integrated terminal at Ahmedabad ready by October 2030.
PVC: 1 MMTPA plant at Mundra, about INR 26,000 crore, 60% spent.
demand_pricing: Navi Mumbai international: IndiGo announced 12 new routes (December to April), Air India Group 7 and Akasa 1, a total of 19 international routes including one existing; 18 international flights, about 3 million passengers a year, announced to move from existing Mumbai airports.

Non-aero growth of 57% YoY drivers: digital penetration (about 25% of non-aero transactions), premiumised shops, new lounges, Navi Mumbai ramp-up, one-off hangar sale in Q2 and ground handling (INR 339 crore in H1, not present in the base period).
Solar: 56% of Q2 sales were rooftop; domestic demand fully absorbed export intake; management says the order book is full for both solar and wind but gave no figures.
Solar Q2 realisations fell QoQ but EBITDA per unit rose, mainly due to about INR 89 crore from closing advance authorisations in Q1.

Copper: EBITDA margin on revenue of 7-8.5% in the recent period, helped by higher by-product (sulphuric acid) prices; long-term band 4-6%. Procurement: 50-60% long-term contracted, plus 20% short-term; offtake of 12-15% assured through two in-house copper tube JVs.
Data centre rentals: some increase over the last six months, not material; ROCE stated as stable.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Navi Mumbai traffic, yield and cost milestones over the next 12-15 months?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to 19 international routes announced and a run rate of 5 million passengers per quarter by Q1 FY28, which it says equals full capacity.

qa_highlights.question: How will the data centre commissioning, capex and equity funding work?
qa_highlights.answer: Operational capacity of 120-150 MW at FY27 exit and about 500 MW over 12-18 months; funding about 20/80 to 30/70, with capex in line with peers since AdaniConneX covers core and shell and MEP only.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the road ramp-up slower than expected, and when will it catch up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said numbers are slightly below its own estimates because of monsoon and northern floods in Q2, and expects to catch up over the next two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Phase 2 Navi Mumbai capex being deferred given weak traffic?
qa_highlights.answer: Not deferred: Phase 2 design is under way with an international consultant, and Terminal 2 Phase 2 construction starts November 2026.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex run rate for the next 3-5 years?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 35,000-40,000 crore a year, led by airports, data centres and PVC; management declined to give EBITDA or margin guidance for FY27 or FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will airlines' reluctance to move to Navi Mumbai affect the airport business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the T1 redevelopment timeline is fixed from April 2027, that one or two airlines may stop flying to Mumbai for a few years, and that this should have almost no impact on total passenger count.

qa_highlights.question: What is the risk on data centre capex per MW and rental rates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said capex increases are passed into billing for new sign-ups, rates are broadly stable, and specific take-or-pay terms will be checked after legal review.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Jaypee asset (JAL) exposure for AEL?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said none of the JAL acquisition remains with AEL; the implementing entity was Adani Infra (India) Limited, and AEL has contributed no equity or funding to the hotels or land projects.

risks_watch: Navi Mumbai ramp: management targets a run rate of 5 million passengers per quarter by Q1 FY28 and says one or two airlines may stop flying to Mumbai for a few years; T1 redevelopment starts April 2027 and airline decisions were expected within about a month.
Roads ramp-up is slightly behind management's own estimates (monsoon and northern floods); management expects to catch up over the next two quarters.

Data centres: operational capacity must go from 94.6 MW to 120-150 MW by FY27 exit and close to 500 MW over 12-18 months; capex per MW of INR 60-80 crore was raised by an analyst amid commodity and equipment inflation; take-or-pay protections still to be confirmed after legal review.
Copper: utilisation must rise from 64% to 80-85% by FY27 end; current 7-8.5% EBITDA margin is helped by sulphuric acid by-product prices, and management guides a long-term band of 4-6%.
Solar: 2 GW per quarter run rate from next quarter and 6 GW cell lines by FY27 end; ALMM-aligned ingot-wafer build-out of about 8 GW by 2028; no order book figures given.

IRM outlook not given due to coal shortage; Mining Services volume to be at least 10-15% above end of last year; PVC (Mundra, about INR 26,000 crore) first part due next fiscal with 6-9 months of stabilisation; capex run rate INR 35,000-40,000 crore a year.

summary.management_tone: Confident on headline growth and asset ramp-ups (airports, copper, solar, data centres), but cautious on forward numbers: management declined to give FY27 EBITDA or margin guidance and refused IRM outlook. It was evasive on take-or-pay terms and data centre margin breakup, deferring both to later disclosure or legal review.

tone.note: Management was confident on airports, copper, solar and data centre ramp-ups and on the capex run rate, but cautious on forward numbers, declining FY27 EBITDA guidance and IRM outlook; analysts probed Navi Mumbai traffic, data centre capex per MW and take-or-pay terms, and roads ramp-up.
